Alice — thanks for the detailed packet. Summary answers below (high-level; see attached commercial outline workbook for example numbers):

1) Recommended primary billing approach
- Dual-metric ratecard: token-based unit for generation/embedding together with an optional request-concurrency tier for latency-sensitive realtime chat. This lets you optimize for cost (tokens) while guaranteeing latency for interactive flows (concurrency slots).

2) Commit tiers & discounts
- Standard approach: 3-tier commit bands (Pilot / Production / Enterprise) with escalating volume discounts: Pilot (monthly small commit) — no discount; Production (annual commit) — 10–18% discount depending on size; Enterprise (multi-year, >1M tokens/month commit) — 18–28% discount plus pipeline credits. We provide concrete breakpoints in the attached XLSX.

3) Overage & smoothing options
- Burst cushion: short-term burst allowance (typically 10–30% of committed monthly tokens) billed at a modest overage rate (base rate + 25%).
- Smoothing true-up: monthly invoice with quarterly true-up; optional annual true-up for multi-year deals. Volume credits vest monthly and can be applied to surges within a rolling 90-day window.
- Pooling: cross-workload pooling available for single account to avoid penalties between chat/embeddings.

4) Capacity guardrails & surge SLA
- Baseline throughput: we can commit to per-second token throughput aligned to commit band (e.g., 200 tok/s per 1M monthly commit) with a measured p95 latency SLO.
- Surge capacity: guaranteed burst capacity (configurable) with automated fallback to compatible model variant if capacity constraints occur. Enterprise Dedicated customers get formal SLA credits for missed throughput targets.

Next steps: I attached Redwood_Commercial_Outline_20270516.xlsx with illustrative numbers and two proposed term sheets (12-month and 36-month). If that aligns, I can convert a chosen term sheet into your SOW template and initiate procurement redlines.

Attachments: Redwood_Commercial_Outline_20270516.xlsx

Diego — reviewed. Quick thoughts:  

- Discount ladder: 36-month multi-year can reach 30% BUT must be conditioned on a minimum annualized commit and an early-termination clawback (standard). We'll offer a stepped vesting: 50% of the multi-year discount applies in year 1, 100% after year 2, to protect us on churn.
- Burst / overage: +25% over base list is fine for immediate burst. For sustained overages (>2 months above 110% of committed average) we prefer to trigger a renegotiation rather than continue paying at overage rates.
- Credits / smoothing: 90-day rolling credit window OK. Credits will be non-refundable and applied to future invoices; cannot be converted to cash.
- Throughput mapping: Karthik to confirm exact tok/s per commit band. If they need hard throughput SLAs we should push them to Dedicated (reserved capacity). Otherwise we give a best-effort SLO with SLA credits for enterprise band.

Karthik — please add your throughput verification inline and I'll finalize the two term sheets.

-Marissa
VP, Commercials
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-17T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: RFP: Commercial/pricing questions + attachments

Confirmed on throughput mapping — we used conservative model. Details:  
- Baseline mapping: 1M committed tokens/month ≈ 200 tok/s sustainable for interactive flows assuming 1x average concurrency of 1.2 and typical sequence lengths (see model assumptions in sheet).
- For latency-sensitive chat (p95 target < 400ms): recommend concurrency slot add-on priced per slot/month; each slot roughly maps to additional reserved capacity that increases committed tok/s by ~250 tok/s.
- If customer needs deterministic per-request latency guarantees at scale, we recommend Redwood Dedicated with an explicit GPU pool; that is what we back into SLA credits for missed throughput ramps.

I'll incorporate these numbers into the XLSX and return a final version for you to send.

-Karthik
Sr. Product Manager, Pricing
